version.changelog: Generalized for any Ollama setup - host now configurable via OLLAMA_HOST env var (defaults to localhost:11434)

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ollama-local
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle is designed to manage and interact with local Ollama models. All Python scripts (`scripts/ollama.py`, `scripts/ollama_tools.py`) use standard `urllib.request` to communicate with a user-configured Ollama host, which is essential for their stated purpose. Crucially, the `run_code` tool within `scripts/ollama_tools.py` is explicitly a mock implementation and does not execute arbitrary code, preventing a significant potential vulnerability. The markdown files (`SKILL.md`, `references/models.md`) provide clear instructions and documentation without any evidence of prompt injection attempts or malicious directives for the agent. There is no indication of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or persistence mechanisms.

llm.summary: This skill is a straightforward Ollama helper, but users should only point it at trusted Ollama servers because prompts are sent to the configured host.

dimensions.detail: Using OLLAMA_HOST is proportionate for an Ollama client, but remote HTTP endpoints are documented without a privacy warning, so prompts, system messages, embedding text, and tool-loop data may leave the machine if configured remotely.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, package installation, remote payload retrieval, or post-install execution was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives explicit CLI/API examples and does not contain prompt hijacking or hidden agent-control instructions; it lacks explicit allowed-tool frontmatter, so users should understand it expects shell execution of the bundled scripts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, or background service behavior was found; the rm command can delete a local Ollama model when explicitly invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is managing and using Ollama models, and the artifacts implement or document model listing, pulling, removal, chat, generation, embeddings, tool-use examples, model guidance, and OpenClaw sub-agent usage.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running the included Python helper scripts. Keep OLLAMA_HOST on localhost for private work, or use only a trusted remote Ollama server with appropriate transport protections. Avoid sending secrets in prompts or embedding text, and verify the model name before using rm because it deletes a local Ollama model.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The environment-derived value is used as the Ollama API base URL, not sent as a credential payload; posting prompts to the configured Ollama endpoint is expected for this client, though remote hosts must be trusted.
[E1] expected: The direct curl examples transmit request bodies to $OLLAMA_HOST, which is core Ollama API behavior and is disclosed in the skill instructions.
[T09] expected: The plaintext remote-host risk is real when OLLAMA_HOST is set to a non-local HTTP server, but the behavior is visible and user-configured rather than hidden exfiltration.
[SQP-2] expected: Model removal is part of the stated model-management purpose and requires an explicit rm invocation, but the documentation and helper script do not add a confirmation warning.
[SDI-4] expected: The example tools advertise realistic capabilities such as web search and code execution, but inspection shows these are mocked responses rather than actual web access or code execution.
[TP4] expected: The apparent mismatch is downgraded after full-package inspection: tool use is implemented in ollama_tools.py, model selection is in references/models.md, and OpenClaw sub-agent integration is provided as usage guidance.
[LP3] unexpected: No explicit allowed-tools or permissions declaration was present; this is a packaging clarity gap, not evidence of hidden or excessive behavior in the artifacts.
